findings.reason: a node dispatched for §25 reads a second deliverable in its own heading that its body and write path no longer own, which re-merges the two goals single_goal-1 separated.
findings.text: §25's heading reads "A parsed review at a head wins over an incomplete one, and a committed record can be repaired", but the repair deliverable is now §26 and §25's body, done-when and write paths hold only the selection change

findings.reason: a node that synthesises the fixture in the host staging store cannot reproduce the stated control (glob order is directory-entry order), so its negative control measures nothing or reports flakily, and the done-when must name a temporary repository/committed docs tree and say the sorted order is the committed caller's.
findings.text: §25's negative control is "the current first-in-sorted-order selection makes the first case refuse when the incomplete record sorts first", but `_select_stored_record` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:414`) does not sort: the committed caller passes `sorted(run_directory.glob("*.json"))` (`review_records.py:589`) while the staging caller passes the bare path plus an unsorted `glob` (`review_records.py:621-626`), so the control has no deterministic order unless the fixture puts both records in a committed docs tree, and the done-when names only "a temporary crew home"

findings.reason: as written, a node satisfies "the record reads superseded afterwards" only by reading the file directly, while the gate reads through the selection and still sees the old status; the section must say where the as-delivered copy goes (outside the committed run directory) or how selection skips it, and that second fix lives in `reckon/crew/review_records`/`review_records.py`, outside the declared write paths.
findings.text: §26 says the repair "writes the repair where the record lives", but `repair_run_review` writes `preserved = source.with_name(source.stem + ".asdelivered.json")` beside the source (`reckon/crew/review.py:3366`), and the committed reader selects from `sorted(run_directory.glob("*.json"))`, where `<review-run>.at-<head>.asdelivered.json` sorts before `<review-run>.at-<head>.json`; both carry the same head, so `_select_stored_record` returns the preserved, still-unsuperseded copy and the gate keeps refusing

findings.reason: without a stated resolution rule the node must either infer the project from the path shape (a rule the `--project` cross-check exists to avoid) or edit `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, which is not in §26's declared write paths, and it must relax the filename guard §26 never mentions.
findings.text: §26 requires `crew repair --review` to accept "the run's committed review location" but does not say how `repair_run_review` identifies it: the function takes no `--project` (`reckon/crew/review.py:3302`), the CLI's `--project` is only a cross-check because `crew_repair` calls `_accept_a_matching_project(run_id, project)` without passing its resolved result (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1323`), and the committed root needs the project (`committed_review_root(project)`), while a committed record's filename is the *review* run id, so the existing `source.name.startswith(reviewed_run_id)` guard also refuses it

rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections name "logs under the run directory", the crew run directory that survives the run, and the new test files are repository paths.
